key_insight: MedDEx shows that for guideline-based clinical decisions, combining LLM-based patient-state extraction with deterministic rule execution can be more accurate and efficient than adding more LLM reasoning steps.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve treatment-planning support by making guideline adherence more reliable while lowering computational cost.
method: LLM extracts structured patient state from clinical records.
A deterministic rule engine executes guideline-defined decision logic.
LLM helps generate plans, but does not replace the rule-based decision step.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated across multiple clinical guideline benchmarks and reported higher decision accuracy with lower inference costs.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate patient-state extraction and well-specified rules, so errors in either component could affect real-world deployment.
paper_title: More Reasoning Is Not Always Better: Executing Clinical Guidelines with LLMs and Rules
